name: setpoint_step_no_derivative_kick
description: setpoint steps from 0 to 5; measurement never moves. PID.c's comment says the derivative is computed on measurement, 'therefore minus sign in front of equation', specifically so a setpoint change alone never excites it (avoiding 'derivative kick', a classic PID design point). This asserts differentiator_state is exactly 0 for the whole run -- a precise, code-derived invariant that no XML dependency declaration could state on its own (contrast with 02, where moving measurement instead does excite it).

metadata.derived_from: src/PID.c PIDController_Update, the comment on derivative-on-measurement
metadata.author: Claude (Sonnet 5), reading the source directly

checks.description: Must stay exactly 0: the derivative term never sees a setpoint change, only a measurement change.
